utterances.speaker: NIHAD REBIHIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: You never were a member of the SDA party, were you, Mr. Rebihic?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REBIHIC
utterances.text: No, I was not.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: You lived for a long time in the area of Vitez, Mr. Rebihic, and, on that basis, you knew the accused Mario Cerkez for a long time; is that true?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REBIHIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: Could you tell us, roughly, when you met Mr. Cerkez for the first time?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REBIHIC
utterances.text: I knew Mr. Cerkez for a long time and we had direct contact when I joined the secretariat of internal affairs in Vitez. And Mr. Cerkez was working in the Territorial Defence staff of Vitez at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: Mr. Cerkez, before the conflict, was working within the Territorial Defence as an assistant for the MTS service, that is, materiel and materiel equipment of the explosives factory called Unis?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REBIHIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: Do you remember a conversation that you had with Mr. Sefkija Djidic in the course of 1992, when this gentleman spoke to you about certain things that Cerkez had done in connection with the weapons under his control?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REBIHIC
utterances.text: Yes. In the course of 1992, it was already quite clear that weapons were being distributed, weapons that were the property of various socially-owned companies, including weapons owned by the Ministry of the Interior. And talking to Sefkija, I learned that in the Unis plants, the weapons were also being distributed. Among others, he mentioned Mr. Cerkez as being one of those who distributed those weapons probably to the HVO or to Croats.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: While working in the police in Vitez, were you informed of the arrest of Cerkez and his involvement in connection with this materiel?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I think that this question is going only on character discrimination of the witness [sic]. It has nothing to do with the case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Indeed, I suppose the relevance is that it's alleged that it was the stealing of equipment, and I take that to be military equipment, but I agree with you that it doesn't seem to take the case much further to note anything else about it. Mr. Lopez-Terres, the accused was arrested. Was he charged with an offence? Is that alleged?

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] He was under interrogation by the police, and that is when Mr. Rebihic met Cerkez and spoke to him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. I've read the summary, and I don't think it's going to assist us very much to hear about that interview. It seems probable that it's best to pass on from this information.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: You were informed, Mr. Rebihic, of the appointment of Mario Cerkez as assistant commander of the Stjepan Tomasevic Brigade and, later on, as commander of the Vitez Brigade?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REBIHIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: At the time that Mario Cerkez was second in command of the Stjepan Tomasevic Brigade, was he stationed in Vitez or in Novi Travnik?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REBIHIC
utterances.text: The headquarters of that brigade was in Novi Travnik, but units and members came from the territory of Vitez, and they were often in Vitez, in the hotel.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: When the conflict broke out, after that you had several contacts with Mr. Cerkez by telephone or direct meetings with him. Could you tell us, what was the reason for these contacts with Mr. Cerkez at that time?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REBIHIC
utterances.text: In the territory of the municipality, tensions had already heightened, and the situation had become quite unbearable as a result of acts committed by members of the HVO; breaking into apartments, seizure of armaments, stopping people at checkpoints, taking people into custody to the police, confiscating weapons, vehicles, money. And in such a situation, the need was felt for contact with those responsible. I was among those who had contact on several occasions with Mr. Cerkez both by phone and, on a number of occasions, in person. I can't tell you exactly when that was. I asked that these activities be halted, and seeking his assistance in liberating people, restoring property, and those were the contacts that I had with Mr. Cerkez.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: You just told us that you contacted Cerkez each time HVO forces were involved in acts committed against Muslims. Did you contact Cerkez also in connection with acts attributed or committed by members of the HOS or the Vitezovi?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REBIHIC
utterances.text: There were regular contacts with Mr. Cerkez regardless of which units were involved, because we felt that Mr. Cerkez was in a position to act and to assist in clearing up the situation and overcoming the incidents that were occurring.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: In the course of this period we're talking about, did you have occasion to contact Darko Kraljevic?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REBIHIC
utterances.text: I never had any contact with Darko Kraljevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: In the course of these contacts and meetings with Cerkez, were you able to notice any particular character traits or a characteristic way of responding to your demands?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REBIHIC
utterances.text: As tensions had heightened in the territory of the municipality, and in view of the acts of HVO members against Muslims, in contacts with Mr. Cerkez one could clearly note a certain overbearing attitude, arrogance. This was nothing serious for him. But he would very frequently accuse the other side, that is, the BH army, and he would justify such acts by the HVO by acts committed by the army, though in truth, in all cases there was no justification. Once, personally in the office, I think I came with the deputy commander, Mr. Badzo, regarding certain agreements reached between representatives of the HVO, the army, the political structures of the HVO, and the coordinating board for the protection of the interests of Muslims, as it was called at the time, and, according to that agreement, all checkpoints were to be removed, free movement, free passage ensured, and materiel and technical equipment restored to their owners, and vehicles which had been confiscated, and also mention was made of a couple of killings that had already occurred, because even before the outbreak of the conflict, a certain number of Muslims had been killed in a very brutal manner. For instance, in Nadioci, Salkic, Trako Samir. Mr. Cerkez would hear us out, but from his behaviour, his gestures, and the expressions on his face, he didn't seem to attach much significance to all this. He just brushed these things off. Agreements were never implemented or carried out as agreed at these meetings.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: Did you ever hear the accused Mario Cerkez making insulting or racist remarks regarding Muslims?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REBIHIC
utterances.text: As a coordinator of the Visoko-Travnik battlefront facing the Yugoslav army and their supporters, in May 1992 I came on leave to Vitez and then I was co-opted to the staff. On that day, there was a review of the HVO at the stadium, which I did not attend, but on the local Vitez television this was broadcast. And on that occasion, I heard clearly Mr. Cerkez addressing the units, say that the Croatian people were under threat, that they must prepare themselves, that there was a danger of them being attacked by the Muslims. That is what I remember Mr. Cerkez saying.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: My question was a simple one. Did Mario Cerkez ever make any racist remarks regarding the Muslims of Bosnia? We are going to speak about that speech later.

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REBIHIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: But you never heard any insults on the part of Cerkez against the Muslims; are we agreed on that?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REBIHIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: You have just referred to a speech that may have been made by Mario Cerkez at the time. We are going to show a videotape, a short abstract of that film, lasting a few seconds, and I will ask you to comment on that event after that. I have to say that the video we are going to show is Exhibit Z2771. Could the first few pictures be in slow motion, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you stop there, please. Thank you. Now we can go on.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We can go on at normal speed now, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Is there a transcript of what was just being said?

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The commentary, according to information that I have, has nothing to do with the pictures that have been shown. We don't have a transcript of this film, which is much longer. This was just a clip that I thought was relevant for what we were discussing today.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I beg your pardon. I fully agree with your question. I think that every video, if we have the sound and the picture, they constitute a whole. And it is up to all of us to assess whether the sound is related to the picture or not. So I would ask for the transcript too.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. But you could probably understand it. What were they talking about?

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It was rather fast, so I didn't quite understand. But, in any event, that sound is linked to the picture shown, or perhaps an even better question would be, could we be given the whole tape, the whole videotape, and then we would be able to say whether the sound is linked to these pictures or some others that we didn't see.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: We shall ask for a transcript of that portion which we've been shown. And the defence should have the whole video. That can be done in due course.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Yes. It's envisaged, yes. We'll do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: You saw this clip, Mr. Rebihic. This brief ceremony that we saw, is that the one that was shown on Vitez television?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REBIHIC
utterances.text: Yes, only there was much more footage in the introduction. Anto Marijanovic spoke, and then in the front row there was Anto Valenta. I recognise him. I recognise Mr. Kordic, though I only know him by sight. I would see him at those press conferences. We never had any personal contact. I recognise Mr. Cerkez, who was touring the units. But there is no question that Mr. Cerkez did address the rally on that occasion.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: The speech of the accused Mario Cerkez that you referred to a moment ago, was it made on the occasion of this ceremony in Vitez?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REBIHIC
utterances.text: Yes. After the units had been reviewed, he addressed the units with a brief speech that I have already referred to.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: Throughout the conflict and, to be more precise, from September 1992 until February 1994, you held a personal diary, several diaries, in which you noted the majority of the events which you considered to be important and which occurred in the municipality of Vitez?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BENNOUNA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Before going onto that question, Mr. Lopez-Terres, what is the relevance? I didn't quite understand the relevance of this video. Why did you show us this video, exactly? For us to understand the meaning?

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I may explain the position of the Office of the Prosecutor. This is the only video that we have, and which shows the ceremony organised in Vitez in the summer of 1992 on the occasion of the oath-swearing ceremony of the local brigade, which was attended by Cerkez as brigade commander, and also by the accused Kordic, as the witness recognised on the tape. This was a ceremony held at the Vitez stadium, which was referred to already by other witnesses, and this was an abstract that we were able to select.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BENNOUNA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So if you are showing us this, it is the ceremony of the oath-taking ceremony of the Vitez Brigade when a speech was delivered by the accused?

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But we don't have the speech.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BENNOUNA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The accused Mario Cerkez is reviewing the troops in the presence of the other accused Dario Kordic, and Anto Valenta.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is all that we have in our possession, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: As I have just said, you kept personal diaries during the conflict and you gave The Office of the Prosecutor abstracts from that diary which you considered to be the most relevant for that period. Those documents have been provided to the defence. I should like you to look once again at a copy of those abstracts to confirm whether they are indeed the documents you gave us. These personal diaries are Exhibit Z2770.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes, one moment. Now, let's try and hurry. Yes, what is it, Mr. Kovacic?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: I'm afraid we have a problem with that. It is clearly -- this diary indeed, the material we get consists of clippings from supposedly an original document. So those are selected parts from a diary. It should be either the whole or nothing, I think.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Provided you've got the original. There is no reason why we should be burdened with a lot of irrelevant material. Mr. Lopez-Terres, what's the position?

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Office of the Prosecutor has communicated to the defence the only exhibits it has possession of. The office of the Prosecution does not have possession of the original, nor the entirety of the notebooks kept by Mr. Rebihic. These excerpts were selected by Mr. Rebihic himself when he met with our investigator at the end of last year. Mr. Rebihic, according to what he told me, is ready to submit those notebooks to the Trial Chamber, if necessary.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Let us get on with what we've got. Now, you've handed over, have you, to the Defence, everything which you yourself have, Mr. Lopez-Terres?

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Absolutely so, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Now, while it's being handed round -- hand it round, please. While that's being done, Mr. Lopez-Terres, we've already had a lot of evidence about Vitez and events in Vitez, and I notice that the witness, between now and, I think, roughly paragraph 64, is going to deal with those. I recollect a document which has gone in which describes all the alleged misdemeanours in Vitez, a summary which we already have. Now, we don't need to go all over that again. I don't remember that it was challenged or not challenged in any detail. Is there anything in here which you want the witness particularly to deal with, which hasn't been dealt with elsewhere?

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I should simply like the witness to confirm that these are indeed excerpts from his notebooks.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, may I address the Court?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Kovacic, you may, but shortly, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The witness, as he says himself, was an intelligence officer and he has selected from his diaries pages or parts of pages and given them to the Prosecutor. As a result, we do not have a complete picture of events, but only the events that he wants to tell us about, and not other events that are linked to these, for us to be able to understand what it's all about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: And that, no doubt, is true, but the time that's being taken up by these sterile debates -- it's a matter, isn't it, for us to decide what weight, if any, we give to these extracts. A witness cannot be forced to produce a personal document like a diary. No doubt, you would like to see it, but we cannot force him to produce it. We have here what are his extracts. Are you objecting to their production?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Very well. We'll consider that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BENNOUNA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Kovacic, you are objecting, if I understand, to this document because they are abstracts. But that does not prevent you yourself to ask additional information about the document as a whole, about the information collected by the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, of course, I will, in accordance with your decision, ask the witness about other parts of that diary.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Well, we think there is force in the objection which Mr. Kovacic made; that this is a selective document, it doesn't necessarily reflect the whole. It would, of course, be possible to ask the witness to produce the rest of it, which he may or may not object to, we don't know. But it seems to us that the fairest way to deal with it, and in order to try and speed things up, is not to have it exhibited, but to allow the witness to refer to it on any matters as an aide-memoire in order that he can recollect or can have access to what he recorded at the time, if he needs to recollect any events. So he can have the document in front of him, and if he needs to refer to it at any time, then of course he can do so. But, as I say, Mr. Lopez-Terres, there is no need to deal at length with events in Vitez which are prior to the conflict which we have had evidence about, unless there are particular matters which you wish this witness to deal with, or in relation to the accused.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The witness was quite ready to give his notes to the Chamber. If the Chamber wishes to see them, they may see them. And the witness can also consult. I mean, there has never been a problem with him. He was quite ready to do so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: But we've ruled on the matter. We are not concerned about that. He can look at the diary to refresh his memory. Yes. I make it plain that whatever the number of the diary is, it is not admitted into evidence, so remove it from the list of exhibits. It's this one, and we'll give it to you back. It's this one, the second one, 2771. There were some other exhibits which you gave us, Mr. Lopez-Terres; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... 9651 and 2770?

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. These are different documents, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. Let's go on.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: On the 19th of October, 1992, Mr. Rebihic, did you observe the concentration of HVO forces in Vitez which then proceeded on to Novi Travnik?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REBIHIC
utterances.text: Yes. If I may dwell on this for a while, Your Honours, that day I was moving about Vitez, as usual, to the seat of the Territorial Defence headquarters which was in the secondary school centre, and as I was passing by the hotel and the municipal hall, I saw quite a number of motor vehicles and quite a number of HVO members. And among other people -- in one of the trucks of the Raba make, I noticed an entire aircraft cannon, and I saw that one of these vehicles were trailing a gun. And they were all concentrated in front of the cultural and artistic society, by the petrol pump in front of the hotel, next to the police building. We already by that time had information that the HVO units were attacking at the time Novi Travnik, so I was monitoring the situation until about 13.00 or half past 12.00, when HVO units, members of HVO units, took some passenger cars and two [indiscernible] vehicles. They boarded them and left in the direction of Travnik. Some of the troops, especially those who were in those trucks, had masks over their faces and were under full combat gear and with full armament. So quite naturally, when I returned to the headquarters, I reported all that to the commander so that they would also know what was going on.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: At that time, did you know that at least 27 soldiers from Vitez were participating in the Novi Travnik attacks on the 19th and the 20th of October, 1992?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REBIHIC
utterances.text: Yes. After that conflict between the HVO and army units in Novi Travnik, from the Territorial Defence staff in Novi Travnik we did receive information with the names of people from Vitez who had taken part in these attacks. And, yes, I believe it was 27 -- could be 27 people. And I just noted it down in my diary, because this is more a personal diary than a diary of an intelligence officer, as it was said a while ago.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: These 27 names can be found in your diary, in the document that you have before you. Are those the names?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REBIHIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, and this is my handwriting. I wrote that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: What is the objection now, Mr. Kovacic?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: It is a page from the diary which you just said --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: He's allowed to look at it to confirm those are the names. Now, that is all. Yes. You're not seeking to produce this, I take it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I really have a problem to understand how is it the witness may and may not use his diary at one and the same time?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: It is perfectly plain. The witness can look at the document and refresh his memory. He's not allowed to produce it in evidence. Now, those are the 27 people. Right. Now let's move on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BENNOUNA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Excuse me. Mr. Kovacic, it is quite clear that in the cross-examination you can do the same thing, that is, you have the same right to ask the witness to refresh his memory, if necessary, by looking at his diary during the cross-examination, so that there is full equality provided. And that is necessary, of course, between the Prosecution and the Defence. You will have the same right then.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: Mr. Rebihic, according to information, two soldiers from Vitez were killed during those conflicts in Novi Travnik; is that so?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REBIHIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: Between the 19th and the 20th of October, 1992, there was a meeting which was held at the Territorial Defence headquarters between the representatives of the two parties to the conflict. Could you tell us what happened at the end of that meeting?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REBIHIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, may I just say a few words about that meeting before I describe its end?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: In a few words.

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REBIHIC
utterances.text: That meeting was called because the conflict in the municipality was escalating. At the time of the development in Novi Travnik, in Vitez, army units were attacked, and in Ahmici a member of the army was killed. It was the result of the roadblocks set up by the HVO in order to prevent people from arriving. So that was why the meeting was convened, and it was called by the UNPROFOR and the ECMM monitoring mission, and Mr. Cerkez was also present at the meeting. It was agreed there that the next day the situation should be calmed down, that all those checkpoints should be lifted and so on and so forth. Now, at the beginning of the meeting itself, HVO representatives and the European Monitors and others went. I do not think they went back to the base. But right next to the school, I believe, an APG was fired from at the room in which the meeting was being held, that is, where the TO headquarters was, but fortunately --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: I'm going to stop you now. If Mr. Lopez-Terres wants to ask about anything in particular in relation to the meeting, he can do that. Yes, Mr. Lopez-Terres.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: And these shots, that is, a rocket fired at the building of the TO headquarters, it happened as soon as the HVO delegation had left; is that so? They ensued immediately afterwards?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REBIHIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: And the Muslim delegation was still there in the building, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REBIHIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: On the 20th of October, that is, a bit later on, there was another meeting which was organised in the building of the post office in Vitez, and it was attended by the accused Mario Cerkez, and your chief was also there? I mean Sefkija Djidic was present there, wasn't he?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REBIHIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: And during that meeting, the building of the TO headquarters in which you were was attacked?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REBIHIC
utterances.text: Yes, but -- and its rear part had already been taken, and some of the members had already been taken into custody and taken away.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: So then you called, by telephone, your superior, Sefkija Djidic, and you explained the situation to him?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REBIHIC
utterances.text: Yes, because HVO units were coming close to the secondary school building where I was with some 30 soldiers, and fire was opened directly -- fire was directly at the building, window panes broken, and simply we feared that people might get killed. So that was when I called the commander, knowing that he was at a meeting in the post office building. I told him about what was going on. And since the line was still open, I could hear Commander Sefkija turn to Mr. Cerkez and tell him what was going on at that moment around the Territorial Defence headquarters, and I could also hear Mr. Cerkez say, very loudly, that those were not his units. And not waiting then, I cut in and I told the commander that I was not interested in whose units they were, and unless this was prevented, and unless this siege was lifted, and unless the fire was put a stop to, that we would have to defend ourselves, that is, return the fire.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: It is quite true that a few moments after that telephone conversation, the fire stopped and the attackers retreated?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REBIHIC
utterances.text: Yes. I forgot to say that. It was hardly any time at all after that conversation the assault stopped and the attackers withdrew.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: The accused Mario Cerkez, during that telephone conversation you could hear Mario Cerkez tell Sefkija Djidic that those were not his units who were participating in the attack. Now, according to Mario Cerkez, whose units were they?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REBIHIC
utterances.text: What I overheard -- while I was talking to my commander, I could overhear Mario Cerkez say that those were not his units and that they were Darko Kraljevic's units, and that is why I angrily retorted that I really couldn't care less whose units they were but simply that the fire had to be stopped.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: During the ensuing period, that is, late 1992 and January 1993, were there Muslim businesses which were damaged, were there crimes committed against them?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REBIHIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: And you recorded all those incidents in your diary, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REBIHIC
utterances.text: As much as I could, depending on the information I had and on what I could hear. But, yes, yes, quite a number, quite a number, quite a number of these incidents were recorded.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: In late 1992, early 1993, you received a report according to which Herzegovinian soldiers, that is, soldiers from Herzegovina, arrived in Vitez. How did those soldiers behave?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REBIHIC
utterances.text: According to information we received from citizens, I mean citizens who had the opportunity to see them, whether walking around the city or in various pubs and restaurants, these soldiers were heard to say that they had come -- on one occasion, for instance, we received a report that since General Praljak was to arrive to work towards setting up a joint command between the HVO and the army of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, and that they were there as security for him. Now, on a different occasion, when after a while one again observed those units around, we received reports that, for instance, people from outside the municipality of Vitez, and some were saying from the territory of Herzegovina, had come because HVO combatants had told them that they would not be fighting the Serbs and that they should get ready to fight the Muslims. So these are -- I did not hear that personally. That was the information that reached us.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: And those soldiers from Herzegovina, they stayed in the area of Vitez at least until April 1993; isn't that so?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REBIHIC
utterances.text: Yes, one could see them. One could see them a few days before the attack in the Vitez area, and we received that intelligence, that information through those roadblocks. There were HVO members stopped, army members, or Muslim citizens, and seized their equipment or vehicles and whatnot. And from those citizens who would come to us to report these incidents and asking for help about their property, we also learned that there were still people whom they identified as Herzegovinians, because of their speech, because of the accent, because of the kind of speech they communicated in.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: Do you remember any distinctive insignia that those forces had?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REBIHIC
utterances.text: Well, sometime in the beginning, sometime in early 1993, at the petrol pump, which is near the hunters' lodge, which is near the village of Krecevine. Personally, I was just simply getting some petrol for my vehicle, and in front of the hunters' lodge I saw those insignia. Now, what it looked to me like was an oak -- was like an oak leaf on the left arm, on the shoulder. And later on we received some intelligence from the ground --

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. Thank you very much. Thank you. Could we show the witness the exhibit which has already been produced, Z25621.

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REBIHIC
utterances.text: I think that is an oak leaf. Yes, I think so. It reminds me of an oak leaf. That is why I say it is an oak leaf. That is what it reminds me of.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: Thank you. And during that period of time that we are talking about, end of 1992, two Muslim soldiers were killed and one was wounded on the 19th of November, 1992. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REBIHIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do remember that. They were members of a unit going to the front in Visoko. They had been on a leave and they had dropped by a coffee bar. They were going from Vitez in the direction of Kruscica. It's owner, I don't know his name, but I know that he is a Croat. And this coffee bar is very near the Catholic cemetery in Kruscica and not far from Cerkez's place there. And I believe that Mario Skopljak's house is also somewhere there. So they had dropped by to have a drink and in that coffee shop they met a couple of Croat combatants, so they had a drink. Husein Kargic was among them and Sead Hurem was also there and Minet Akeljic was also the driver. Now, before they left, as they were paying the bill for those drinks, they had -- a group of Croat combatants had come out. And as soon as they left this coffee shop, they waylaid them and, from an ambush, fire was opened on them, and Husein and this Sead Hurem were killed, and the driver was severely wounded and taken to the hospital.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: And after that you did meet with the accused, Mario Cerkez, and you spoke to him about that. Do you remember what kind of a reaction did he produce at the time?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REBIHIC
utterances.text: Well, it wasn't immediately after that, because naturally we had to set up investigation teams to go into that incident. And on one occasion, as we used to set up commissions made of army representatives, HVO representatives, so as to prevent or suppress those kind of incidents. And at one of those meetings I had a chance of seeing Mario. And on that occasion we went through all the incidents in the territorial municipality, including these killings. Not only these two, because there were quite a number of them. And Mario was very cool about that. He almost dismissed it. He just had a very dismissive attitude. My impression was he wasn't really particularly interested in all that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: But to your knowledge, the factor that those crimes were committed against Muslims at the time, was there any investigation? Did the relevant HVO authorities conduct an investigation about those incidents?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REBIHIC
utterances.text: I don't think that any investigation was taken to its end. It will be agreed that an investigation would be either taken, teams would be designated, but they never heeded any result, nor did I ever hear that there has been any prosecution, except in the case of Esad Salkic's murder in Nadioci. When I heard that Miroslav Bralo, called Cico, I think, that he had been taken into custody, arrested, and then he was released when the conflict broke out. And then he also re-emerged in those attacks in the municipality. As for all the other cases, the investigation was never taken to its end. None of those cases were ever fully investigated.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: And this Miro Cico, is that Miroslav Bralo?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REBIHIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: And he was one of the HVO Vitez?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REBIHIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: Do you recall, Mr. Rebihic, in January 1993, a message that you received according to which units from Busovaca were preparing to leave for Gornji Vakuf?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REBIHIC
utterances.text: I think that through the communications links this was discovered. A message was being conveyed from Zenica, I think, that units were preparing from Busovaca and Zenica that were to pass through Vitez, in the direction of Gornji Vakuf, because the HVO had already carried out an attack in Gornji Vakuf against army units.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: On the 27th of January, 1993, do you remember that HVO soldiers entered a class and forced Muslim students to stand for about a quarter of an hour?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REBIHIC
utterances.text: We were informed about this by the children's parents, because children at the time were going to school together. And we were told, I think it was five soldiers, Croat soldiers, entered the classroom and demanded that Muslim children get up and to remain standing for quite some time.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: That same day you also received information according to which five mini-buses with HVO soldiers from Vitez were going to Busovaca?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REBIHIC
utterances.text: Yes. The HVO attack had already started in Busovaca and, as was customary, highly mobile HVO units existed. We noticed, with documents that corroborated this, that five mini-buses with HVO soldiers in them had left in the direction of Busovaca. We assumed that they were going to their assistance.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: Do you remember the disarming of Muslim guards of the Unis factory at the beginning of March, 1993?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REBIHIC
utterances.text: Yes. A rumour spread in Vitez that new HVO members had arrived and the security service in Princip, that is the SPS Vitezit plants, that members of Muslim ethnicity working in the security service were disarmed one evening and they were no longer allowed to perform their duties. Apparently the security would be provided by the regional police, they were told.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: That same day a Croatian flag was hoisted in front of the factory; was it not?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REBIHIC
utterances.text: Yes, that same day at the gates, and the whole length of the gate, a Croatian flag was hoisted. This normally irritated the workers because they felt that this was a systematic effort to impose the authority of the Croatian community of Herceg-Bosnia, which we were already familiar with, and that HVO authority was permeating all levels of power.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: You already briefly referred to this, but do you remember the 4th of April 1993 in the presence of soldiers external to Vitez that called themselves the Tigers?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REBIHIC
utterances.text: Yes. This was also information received from the ground, which we received from people who saw this concentration of these soldiers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: There is an objection.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very briefly. This is the 6th or 7th answer of the witness saying information was received. That information, such information, is based on ordinary rumours. So it is at least double, triple or more hearsay. Information reports are based exclusively on rumours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes, but this witness was receiving these reports, as I understand it, as part of his professional work, and therefore, in my view, he is entitled to tell us about it. Mr. Rebihic, did you receive these reports as part of your work in the Territorial Defence at the time?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REBIHIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: In your diary, at the time you noted the presence of these soldiers called Tigers in Vitez on the 4th of April, 1993.

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REBIHIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: What was the reason for the presence of those soldiers at the time?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REBIHIC
utterances.text: I just remembered. We also had information, I'm sorry, but I have to use that term, information, received from citizens who saw members and who heard directly of them coming to Vitez because the HVO would not wage war against the Serbs, against the former JNA, but that they had come to wage war against the Muslims. I think, as far as I can remember, that the term used, what that was, was that they would slaughter Muslims.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: Could you refresh your memory regarding this entry in your diary of the 4th of April. Could we show the witness.

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REBIHIC
utterances.text: Yes, that is it. That is precisely it. Because of the arrival of General Praljak. I see. I'm sorry. General Praljak was supposed to work on the establishment of a joint command between the HVO and the army, and I think it was then that Dzemal Merdan was appointed on behalf of the army, Franjo Nakic. I can't remember exactly the names of those people, but, in any event, joint command was formed based in Travnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: I think there is a mistake in the French translation. Not a joint commander but a joint command. And these soldiers who -- the Tigers, they came from Croatia?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REBIHIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: And the 12th of April, 1993, you yourself were arrested by the HVO. Could you tell us briefly what happened on that day?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REBIHIC
utterances.text: On the 12th of April, in the morning, I was heading towards Travnik intending to take some medicines or, rather, blood plasma to the hospital in Travnik. At the checkpoint, which was held by the HVO, at the crossroads of the roads between Travnik, Novi Travnik, and Vitez, I was stopped. Smajo Haskic was with me in the car, who was temporarily employed in Switzerland because they had donated the vehicles and medicines and some equipment. I was driving with him. After being stopped, one of the Croatian soldiers, all I know is that he worked in Kajic Drago's cafe in Bila as a waiter. He opened the door of the car, pulled me out onto the road, kicked me in the small of the back twice, took me to a wooden hut to search me. This young man managed to escape. How he did it, I don't know. They were probably focusing on me. He informed others what had happened to me. From there I was taken to Gorazde near the management building of the former railway station. They took me around the back and I found some other men there with their hands tied behind their backs facing the wall. I was forced to do the same. My hands were tied with wire. And we waited a little. They were bringing in more, both civilians and other men. Then they shoved us into a small room, probably a workshop belonging to that company, with broken tables and chairs, remnants of coal and so on. There were more than 30 of us. Anyway, a lot of us. In the afternoon, about 4.00, I think -- no, before that, two Croat soldiers came in, called out names in a vulgar manner, using insults and swear words. In the afternoon we were released. The local HVO commander, I think his name was Keric, that was his surname, he apologised and said it was a misunderstanding. That was when I was released and I returned to the Vitez headquarters. That was the arrest -- my arrest.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: On that day you were travelling in uniform?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REBIHIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: The vehicle that you were driving in, was it confiscated by the HVO?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REBIHIC
utterances.text: The vehicle was seized and everything inside it, the medicine. When I was released, I came across the driver of the medical centre in Vitez. I think his name was Saric. He drove me back. I asked him that we should stop at the crossroads, at the checkpoint where I was arrested, to see whether the vehicle was there. We stopped and we were told that the vehicle had been driven away by Kraljevic, so that we never regained possession of that vehicle. Upon my return to headquarters, I know that my commander contacted the HVO commander, Mr. Cerkez, to regain control of the vehicle. There were promises, but it was never returned to us.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: The people who arrested you on that day --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: We are going to adjourn now. We'll adjourn now 'til 2.30. Mr. Rebihic, would you remember, in this and in any other adjournments there may be, not to speak to anybody about your evidence until it's over. Don't let anybody speak to you about it. We'll adjourn. --- Luncheon recess taken at 1.00 p.m. 20 21 22 23 24 25

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Judge Robinson.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Kovacic, I just wanted to remind you that the Prosecutor did indicate that the diary of the witness would be available for examination, so you might want to consider that, particularly if your cross-examination isn't completed today. You could have a look at it during the evening to see to what extent it could be of assistance.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much for warning me. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: In fact, Judge Robinson's observations rather overtake the matter that I was going to raise. I was simply going to explain to the Court that possibly not a misunderstanding but a technical difficulty had arisen this morning. Because of the witness's quite typical concern, although he's willing, as I understand it, to make his diary available, it goes through the Court in his understanding of things, and so what had happened here was we had served some days ago the excerpts that we had translated into B/C/S and indeed into French, I think, for the convenience of that passage of the evidence, and indeed the concern of the Defence would indeed be met by the matter that Judge Robinson has raised. I simply mention that because when we come on to the detail of the day's events which the witness, I think, chronicled minute by minute, the Chamber may, on reconsideration, think that there would be a quicker way of getting to that evidence than simply taking it by the indirect route of the witness refreshing his memory. I just mention that to see if it's helpful.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: We'll look at it, yes. Yes. Well, let's get on, shall we now.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: Upon your arrest on the 12th of April that we have already discussed, you were arrested by members of the military police, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REBIHIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: Two days later, the 14th of April, 1993, is it true that several Muslims who were going to work in Novi Travnik were arrested by the HVO, and some of them were then detained at the Kaonik camp?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REBIHIC
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct. Workers on their way to work at Bratstvo Company in Novi Travnik, travelling to Novi Travnik, were stopped by the HVO. A number of them were taken off the bus, taken first to Stojkovici, I think, where the camp was known as Kace. Some of them were released, and also some of them were taken to other camps, including the camp at Busovaca.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: Thank you. The next day, the 15th of April, it was the day of the first anniversary of the BH army?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REBIHIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: There were festivities held in Vitez to mark the occasion. Could you tell us quickly what was reported to you at the end of those festivities by Mr. Saban Mahmutovic?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REBIHIC
utterances.text: On that day, a joint meeting was held in Vitez between representatives of the army and the HVO or, rather, the political structures of the HVO and the coordination committee for the protection of Muslims, as it was called then, to calm down the situation and in order to reactivate the civilian police, because the civilian police had been disarmed on two occasions in the police station, that is, police officers of Muslim ethnicity were disarmed. At the headquarters of the TO, while the festivities were still ongoing to mark the anniversary of the formation of the BH army, we were told that they would meet again the next day to discuss the reorganisation of the police and that a joint police force would start operating again, as it had before, and that there was no fear of any further escalation in the territory of the municipalities, that things would settle down after that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: The accused Mario Cerkez, did he participate at that meeting?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REBIHIC
utterances.text: Yes. In observing the anniversary of the army, representatives of the HVO -- military representatives and civilian representatives of the HVO were invited. Among others, I saw Mr. Cerkez, who came to that party, which was a very modest one in line with our possibility. I met with my commander, Sefkija Djidic. They were talking, so I approached, and I knew Cerkez and I was glad to see him, and during that conversation we discussed the replacement of the commander of the 325th Army Brigade. But only then did I hear from Mario that Mensur Kelestura would come as commander of that brigade. As I had known that gentleman in Visoko, where I was with my unit, I said that this was a highly-capable officer, a person with great quality, and because -- the commander of the 325th had to leave because of sickness. Then he told me that he would like to meet with Mr. Cerkez and to play a game of chess with him. I thought that was rather strange. Mario continued talking to the commander, Sefkija. When they departed, I don't know. After that, we stayed on in the headquarters and analysed the activities of the day.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: The evening of the 15th of April, around 20.00 hours, were there movements of troops, of armed soldiers, noticed in front of the cultural centre of Vitez?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REBIHIC
utterances.text: In view of the fact that telephone lines were still operating, we had contact with citizens in town, and from a number of citizens we received reports that they had noticed concentrations of HVO soldiers at the Workers' University, near the hotel, near the civilian police headquarters. Around 20.00 hours, a liaison officer of the British Battalion, Mr. Matthews, came to the TO headquarters and, with great concern, confirmed the same, saying that something must be wrong, that something was in the offing, because he too had seen large concentrations of troops, movement of troops, and simply that he was concerned about the situation on the ground.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: You mentioned, in your diary, this statement regarding the preparation of troops in front of the cultural centre, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REBIHIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: In the morning of the 16th of April, the Muslims of Vitez, did they expect an attack on the part of HVO forces?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REBIHIC
utterances.text: We never believed that an attack would occur, because both the political and the military leadership of the Muslim part sought at all cost to avoid any conflict with the HVO in the area of Vitez, and for several reasons. This is confirmed by numerous negotiations and agreements testifying to those efforts to avoid a conflict. I remember that the coordinating committee for the protection of Muslims, together with the TO staff, had proposed that we accept HVO demands for the army to join the HVO, but the insignia was disputed. They didn't want to wear HVO insignia, but that TO insignia should be allowed. I also remember another detail --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: I am going to interrupt you for a moment. The question, really, was did you expect --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: The question is whether you expected an attack or not. Perhaps you could just answer "yes" or "no," and then if there is any other information which counsel want to ask you about, they can do that --

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REBIHIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: You had information about this concentration of soldiers in front of the cultural centre, but apparently you didn't attach any importance to those movements that evening?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REBIHIC
utterances.text: We didn't. In view of the fact that we were informed that the meeting had been fruitful, that it had resulted in certain agreements, and so we never expected anything to happen. Also another meeting had been scheduled for the next day.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: The 15th of April 1993, were there many soldiers of the Bosnian army present in Vitez?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REBIHIC
utterances.text: Very few.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: Where was the majority of Muslim soldiers, then?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REBIHIC
utterances.text: In view of the fact that the 325th Brigade was in the process of formation by decision of competent bodies, there was one battalion in Preocica, another in Kruscica, and in Stari Vitez there was the TO headquarters which had more of an administrative than a military role. So that in the town itself there were very few men under arms, with the exception of the military police and the civilian police, which, because the army anniversary was being observed, were present and some members who belonged to units that were on their way to the front at Visoko and Vlasic, the Turbe-Travnik front.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: Is it correct that the majority of Muslim units were on the front against the Serbs in the region of Mount Vlasic?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REBIHIC
utterances.text: Yes. Ever since May 1992 we held the front lines towards the former army, the Serbs in Bijelo Bucje and Visoko.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: Were there any HVO forces on your side against the Serbs?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REBIHIC
utterances.text: There were no HVO troops with us, with the exception of 1992, for a time when the artillery at the Mascema were held by them, and they provided some artillery support.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: Let me rephrase my question. In April 1993, as far as you are aware, were there any HVO forces, and specifically those from Vitez, deployed against the Serbs?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REBIHIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: On the 16th of April, in the morning, you said that you were surprised by an attack, which you were not expecting.

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REBIHIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: On that day you mentioned minute by minute, when it was possible, the events that took place, and you mentioned them in your diary; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REBIHIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: In a few words, could you tell us what the main phases of that day, the 2nd of April were. It's being understood that I would like to go back to some of the points that deal with conversations that the accused Mario Cerkez may have had.

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REBIHIC
utterances.text: Factually, minute by minute, I don't think that I would be able to interpret the events of that day. But I know that the attack started at 5.45 a.m. by shelling from artillery pieces in the wider area, including Ahmici, Kruscica. With respect to Old Vitez itself, the first shell was lobed in exactly around 5.45 near the command post of the Territorial Defence headquarters. This was followed by a whole cannonade in the wider area, and also there was mortar fire and various calibre, different calibre, weapons fire. Later on, let's say between 7.00 and 8.00, there was small arms fire which could be heard from the area of Ahmici. One could see smoke and traces of fire. There was sounds of shooting coming from other areas. I also heard, still early in the morning, and I had a radio transmitter called Motorola, a walkie-talkie type of device. I had it on at that time and I actually followed the HVO communications because I was interested in what was going on. On several occasions I could hear the soldiers, and at one point Mr. Cerkez himself, once or twice on that day. In the morning between 8.00 and 9.00, he was informed by a participant that UNPROFOR was coming in the field near the church. Mr. Cerkez responded, and I recognised his voice because I know his voice very well. He cursed -- it was -- he expressed himself in vulgar terms, cursed mother, and he said, "You know what to do." Throughout the day, the operations, the combat operations, were very intense. In the afternoon hours, or perhaps around noon, I again heard Mr. Cerkez communicating with one of the participants in the communication, and this was Marko Lujic. I also recognise his voice. He asked -- and I think he said -- he said, "Could you hit again the same thing you did a moment before." This is the feature J. Since I had been following what was going on, the fire had come from the area of Mosunj, and it hit a target near Jelovac. So "J" I took to stand for Jelovac. Shortly thereafter I could hear detonation and then an explosion. Later I also heard communications of the HVO. I heard this through this Motorola. I overheard them asking for assistance, that is, support in order to neutralise machine guns. I think that it was Marko Livancic who was on the line. They were calling each other by their first names. So the message went, "Marko is seeking assistance to target machine gun nest." I could not clearly determine where it was. Also, in the day, I was able to hear that the HVO was announcing the targeting of the VBR positions, and the fighting went on from early morning 'til about, perhaps, 7.00 in the evening.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: You mentioned, in general terms, the chronology of that day. I would like us to go back more specifically to some of the schedules or time frames. Perhaps you would have to have in front of you the part that I am speaking about in respect of your diary, in which you mentioned all of the events which you have quickly mentioned again, and specifically the conversations in which you recognise Mario Cerkez's voice. Mr. Usher, would you please show the witness, show him this document, which is from his diary, dated 16 April.

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REBIHIC
utterances.text: Yes, this is my handwriting. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: Could you tell us exactly when it was that you recognise the accused Mario Cerkez's voice, and say what he stated at that time?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REBIHIC
utterances.text: From here you can see that this was at 8.30 a.m. that UNPROFOR had arrived in the field from the direction of the church, and the quote itself is, "Fuck their mother. You know the feature. Go on and shoot."

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: Before that conversation, you intercepted messages which it appeared that mosques were the targets?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REBIHIC
utterances.text: Yes. This was at the beginning of these operations. The mosque was the first target. That was the message.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: During the morning at 8.30 also, it says in your diary that you had noticed that there was shooting on the Preocica mosque.

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REBIHIC
utterances.text: Yes. Again, this was -- this was intercepted through their communication lines. It was directed towards Preocica, and you could hear the shell hitting in that area. Also, the mosque in Vitez was hit from the direction of Jaruga. That neighbourhood is called Miklici. Then we had people calling in from town that there were some murders there, that people were being arrested, taken to the camp in the Workers' University, and later they were detained in the forestry building in Rijeka, then in the slaughter house. So on that day there were mass arrests in the territory of the town where the HVO exercised full control of the situation.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: You put all this information down as soon as you received it; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REBIHIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: When one reads your entry for the 16th of April, it says that there were three different reports, three different times. There's a first report at the early morning, the second one at 10.30, and another one at around 18.00 hours in the afternoon. Whom were these reports intended for?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REBIHIC
utterances.text: These reports were sent to the superiors, that is to the brigade headquarters, because we -- organisationally we were part of the 325th Brigade. We were obliged to send regular reports on the situation on the ground so that people would have the full picture of what was going on.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: During the morning you had information which said that well-known people in Vitez had been killed; there was Midhat Varupa and then there was Zlotrg's wife?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REBIHIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Just answer "yes" or "no," for this purpose.

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REBIHIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: You referred to a conversation with a man named Marko Livancic. The conversation, apparently, took place at 11.30 on that morning; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REBIHIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: Did you know that person?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REBIHIC
utterances.text: I did not know Marko Livancic. I knew him from -- we communicated. But somebody on the line said, "Marko Livancic is requesting such and such," and this is what I noted down in the diary.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: The message that you were able to pick up was perfectly audible and clear; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REBIHIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: Around 12.25, there was firing toward the direction of Kruscica, and a few moments later, the BritBat officer, Captain Dundas-Whatley, came to your headquarters and asked that a ceasefire be arranged?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REBIHIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: Did your commander go to that meeting, and could you tell us what he reported when he came back from the meeting?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REBIHIC
utterances.text: The meeting was at the UNPROFOR base in Bila, and after he came back -- that is, the meeting was with the HVO representatives, and obviously he represented the ABiH army. He said that a ceasefire had been arranged, that the units would stay at the positions which they had taken, that all the materiel was going to be turned over, that an exchange of all prisoners was going to take place, and that cessation of all hostilities was to take place.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: You have already referred to the second communication, during which you recognised the accused Mario Cerkez's voice. I would like you to look at the page of your diary which relates to that conversation. Would you reread that passage as it appears regarding the second conversation? Reread it, please, so you can refresh your memory.

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REBIHIC
utterances.text: At 13.17, Mario, because I recognised Mario on the line, he says, "Can you perhaps target the thing you just did a moment ago?" This is above the "K". That is, "K" stands for elevation, and the letter is "J" which I, in brackets, put to stand for Jelovac. Perhaps there is a block here, I think, of something, but it says that, "Target it well."

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: Did this conversation concern Marko Lujic and the accused Mario Cerkez?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REBIHIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: You recognised his voice as well; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REBIHIC
utterances.text: Yes. I also know Marko Lujic quite well, because I had communication with him over a long time and we were even neighbours in the village.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: During that same day, in your diary, you indicated that there was a further shooting on the city of Vitez?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REBIHIC
utterances.text: Yes. Again, during the conversation among the participants on the line, I overheard the one saying, "Tell number 23 to target Jelovac with five projectiles," and here it says, "Number 9." And, "Tell them to do this at 13.40 hours." So that means that that communication took place at 13.40. Then later you see clearly that 13.48, after the firing -- after hearing the firing from the direction of Brajici, the mortar fire was used on Jelovac. Further down, if you can see -- again this is not the communication lines or the BiH army -- from Veceriska it was reported that there were a number of casualties, and the assistance of the army was sought.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: When you mentioned Mario's first name, this is Mario Cerkez, of course; isn't that correct? There weren't any other Marios with whom you might be confused in Vitez?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REBIHIC
utterances.text: Absolutely not, because I do know Mr. Cerkez well because I sat with him on a number of occasions. I knew him over a period of years, and there can be no confusion about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: The artillery firing continued until the evening, around 19.00 hours, that is, on Vitez and its surroundings; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REBIHIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: On the following day, the 17th of April, the attacks resumed -- it was a Saturday -- and continued throughout the day?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REBIHIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: Do you remember that there were several shots that were fired from the Mosunj quarry; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REBIHIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: The next day, on Sunday, the 18th of April, there was more shooting, and during the afternoon you again heard shots coming out of that Mosunj quarry; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REBIHIC
utterances.text: Yes. I think that was 14.08, in the direction of Zenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: Also on that afternoon of Sunday, the 18th of April, while you were in Stari Vitez, you saw a truck. Could you tell us a little bit about that truck and tell us what happened at that point?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REBIHIC
utterances.text: Since no attack was expected, we had no lines of defence in Vitez. After the attack, we obviously wanted to dig in and establish lines of defence. At one point in the afternoon, I went in the direction of the town, that is, to the utilities building, to see whether the army was digging in, and near the mosque a truck came by, a drab olive colour, drove past me, and I knew that it was a fuel tank and I knew that the HVO had one. For a while these -- they had two such trucks, and for a while -- there was an open field near Mario Cerkez's house, and that's where they were parked. I immediately recognised the truck as one of these two trucks. Perhaps 100 metres later, I heard a powerful explosion, and the explosion actually threw me on the ground and I lost consciousness. When I came to, I saw roof tiles and all kinds of debris. I was surrounded by that. I looked farther afield and I saw that several houses were destroyed, many roofs were blown away, and I quickly returned to the headquarters to see what we could do. I assumed that there had been casualties, both dead and wounded.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: After the explosion, six people died; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REBIHIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: I'm going to show you the death certificates. The Office of the Prosecutor only has five death certificates. I would like to ask you to tell us whether these are, in fact, the names of the people who were killed that day. This is Exhibit Z2210-9 from Z221-9 [as interpreted]. These documents were distributed; 2210-9, 2210-13. Would you review those documents and tell us whether these are, in fact, the people who died on that day, as far as you know?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REBIHIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's Husein Karahodza, and the fuel truck did explode right next to --

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: Just say "Yes", please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we show the witness the other death certificates? There are five of them.

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REBIHIC
utterances.text: Mehmed Silnovic, yes, that's one of them. Mujo Sahman, who was identified later on as the driver of the truck. Fatima Grahic, at the moment of -- when we were taking down the information, we didn't realise this was a waitress who was sleeping in the house. But in any event, this is this poor victim. Then Munevera Begovic, that is also correct. It is a young woman. Then Enes Sehic's son and Enes Sehic, they were killed in their house because the explosion threw them out of the house, and in fact this woman was found hanging over the window.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: I have the death certificate for that sixth person, Sehic.

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REBIHIC
utterances.text: Sehic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: There were also quite a number of wounded that day?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REBIHIC
utterances.text: There were a number of wounded.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: After the explosion of the truck, were you told that the population in the centre of Vitez had been informed before the explosion that they should keep their windows open?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REBIHIC
utterances.text: Because some phone lines were still open, we received calls that the population had been advised, even on local television and local media, to keep their windows open because the Muslims would attack, that there would be artillery fire, and in this way the breaking/shattering of windows or glass would be prevented.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: On that day, was there an attack by the Bosnian army against Vitez?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REBIHIC
utterances.text: Shortly after the explosion of the fuel truck, a fairly heavy attack of the HVO followed, but we were able to suppress it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: Before the truck explosion, was there an attack carried out by the BH army in Vitez?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REBIHIC
utterances.text: As a rule, the HVO attacked in the morning and then in the afternoon. It would be artillery fire, and then as far -- and then in the afternoon they would use the small-arms fire.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: You're talking about the HVO, not about the BH army?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REBIHIC
utterances.text: Yes, I'm referring to the attacks of the HVO against Vitez, Stari Vitez, not about the army. The army did not carry out any attacks on that day.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: That's what I wanted to know. This previous information given to the population, was it confirmed to you by Mr. Borislav Jozic, whom you knew at the time?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REBIHIC
utterances.text: Yes. When the mixed commission was formed at the camp or, rather, at the UNPROFOR base in Bila, at one of those meetings, talking to Jozic, he confirmed this for me.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: You had information after the explosion according to which the people who participated in the operation could be Darko Kraljevic and the above-named Marko Lujic?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REBIHIC
utterances.text: That was information received from citizens who came to Stari Vitez and from conversations with them, because at the end of April, through the mediation of General Petkovic, Sefer Halilovic, who came to Vitez, one of the conclusions was to release prisoners on both sides and to make it possible for them to go where they wished. A number of prisoners --

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: It was then that you learned who could have been the perpetrators of that act; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REBIHIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes. This was received in a report from the criminal service and registered as such.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: Very well. Sometime later, you signed a report on the 2nd of June, 1993, mentioning the names of these two people as being behind the explosion. This is Exhibit Z1009,1. Do you recognise that report, Mr. Rebihic?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REBIHIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do. It is a report drafted by the service for suppressing crime in the TO staff and on the basis of information received by the service. I signed it because the person in charge of those activities after the burial of the bodies, as a large number of his family members were killed in Ahmici, was evacuated from Stari Vitez. The commander Sefkija then authorised me to coordinate work with the criminal inspectors and, as the deputy commander, I signed this report which was forwarded to the corps or, rather, the brigade so that they should be informed of the information collected by the staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: This Marko Lujic who is mentioned in this report and whom you have mentioned, is he the same one who had the conversation with Mario Cerkez on the 16th of April at 13.18 hours?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REBIHIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: On the 28th of April 1993, you attended the burial of the bodies of Muslims killed in Ahmici, Nadioci, Vitez, Gacice, Rijeka and Donja Veceriska. Do you remember that event?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REBIHIC
utterances.text: I remember it very well. It is something I shall never forget.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: On that day, 96 bodies of Muslims were buried?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REBIHIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: The Bosnian army handed over four bodies of HVO soldiers to HVO representatives.

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REBIHIC
utterances.text: The number applies to the area of responsibility of the TO staff, and these were killed HVO soldiers who were killed on the first day of the attack on Stari Vitez. Therefore, they were in the territory within the control of the TO staff, and that is why we handed over those bodies to the commission working on the exchange.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: Together with other persons working with you, Ramo Vatres and Enes Djidic, 54 bodies that were buried on that day, how were you able to identify those persons? But in a few words, please.

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REBIHIC
utterances.text: In view of the fact that when we picked up the bodies from the elementary school in Vitez, where we took over those bodies from the civil defence of the HVO, we carried the bodies in a cold storage van and a lorry. Dark was falling, and on the basis of the report we had from the HVO, we checked the report against the bodies. Each body bore a number and it corresponded to the number in the report we had received. In the course of the identification, uncovering the bodies that we were identifying, we would find a document of some kind, an identity card, a birth certificate, or some other kind of certificate. In most cases those data were recorded on the basis of those documents. As darkness was falling very quickly, unfortunately we could not examine all of them and we had to bury them, to put them in a joint grave directly from the truck, and then a list was compiled.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: You established on that day your own list in one of your diaries. I should like to show you that document. It is document Z2770.

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REBIHIC
utterances.text: Yes, that is a list that I wrote, and I think that the Trial Chamber has this list from my previous testimony.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let me draw the attention of the Chamber that the witness has already testified in another case concerning Ahmici, and that this document was admitted during those proceedings.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: I should also like to show you photographs, Mr. Rebihic, that were taken on the occasion of the burial. Will you please tell us whether you recognise the places? These photographs correspond to Exhibit Z2772.

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REBIHIC
