utterances.text: Yes, that is the cemetery where these bodies were buried, very close to Idriz Begovic's house. That is how the bodies were marked. These numbers are identical to the numbers in the list.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: Please have a look at the other photographs. There are six of them in all. Could you show the witness the others as well, please; the other photographs.

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REBIHIC
utterances.text: Here I recognise people if necessary. I can tell you their names. That's when they were unloaded.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: The next photograph, please.

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REBIHIC
utterances.text: I can be clearly seen here. That's me. That is me. Because I was in charge of the burial. That is also me.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: That's all. Thank you. In the course of this burial, you and your two colleagues, Mr. Djidic and Mr. Vatres, you were able to examine some of the bodies, and you were able to establish how those bodies were mutilated, burned or shot with bullets. Could you convey to us what you established on the day of the burial?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REBIHIC
utterances.text: On the day of the burial we took over the bodies which had been dead for some time, so that the whole atmosphere was terrible. There was a very strong stench. However, when examining the corpses, we were able to establish that most of them were killed at close range with firearms, that some of them had burnt, because the bodies were burned beyond recognition. Among them were children. Then there was an elderly person, close to 70, whose neck had been slit. Then we saw another man with a crushed skull. There was just some bones and skin attached to the neck, so that the picture was really horrendous.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: You were also able to see the body of the former chief of police, Saban Mahmutovic. Could you tell us again what you established?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REBIHIC
utterances.text: Saban Mahmutovic was also shot with firearms from the front and from behind, as the entry and exit wounds showed. I think there were 14 or 15 bullet holes that were visible. This occurred in the immediate vicinity of the HVO command, the HVO headquarters.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: Could you tell us anything about the clothing worn by some of those bodies?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REBIHIC
utterances.text: With the exception of two men who had military uniforms on them, the rest were civilians, elderly men and women, children. There were very few men of military age among them.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: Did you note that some of them were still in their pyjamas?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REBIHIC
utterances.text: Yes, that was the case with Salem Topcic, who was brought in a pyjama. When we undid the nylon bag, we saw that he was wearing his pyjamas.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: Salem Topcic was a former policeman in Vitez, was he?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REBIHIC
utterances.text: Yes. He used to work in the crime section of the civilian police in Vitez.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: In the days that followed this first burial, new bodies were entrusted to you coming from Ahmici that were found by soldiers of the UNPROFOR.

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REBIHIC
utterances.text: Yes, members of UNPROFOR. I think it was on the 10th of May that they brought four bodies, they brought them in a totally charred condition. The bodies had been burnt. It was not possible to identify a charred body, but on the basis of the spots where the bodies were found by UNPROFOR soldiers, these were bodies of one family belonging to Sakib Ahmic, his son, daughter-in-law and two grandchildren, one of which was a three-month-old baby.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: The next day, the 11th of May 1993, you were appointed to be a member of a committee for the exchange of bodies and prisoners, a commission whose tasks were defined by the two brigade commanders, Mario Cerkez and Mensur Kelestura. Do you remember that commission?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REBIHIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do. I received an order appointing me on behalf of the army, Safet Hajdarevic from the 325th brigade. I represented the municipal TO staff. The HVO was represented by Mr. Borislav Jozic, a HVO officer, and Mr. Stipo Krizanac. The task of the commission was to work on the exchange of all prisoners, the establishment of the telephone lines, electricity supply system, because Stari Vitez had no telephone lines, nor did it have any electricity any more. In accordance with the tasks specified in the order of appointment signed by Mr. Mario and Mr. Kelestura, we started working.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: When you say Mr. Mario, you mean Mario Cerkez, don't you?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REBIHIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, of course, Mario Cerkez.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: I am going to show you two documents, one dated the 11th of May, the other the 22nd of May 1992, Z903 and Z965.

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REBIHIC
utterances.text: Yes. This is the order on the basis of which the commission was formed, indicating the tasks of the commission and its members.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: On the bottom left of the second page is the signature of Mario Cerkez, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REBIHIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, yes. That is it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: Thank you. After the formation of this commission, you participated in a meeting organised by UNPROFOR and the European Monitoring Mission to allow for an exchange of prisoners of the two warring parties. At the end of this meeting an exchange did in fact take place. The problem of 13 detainees arose at that point. Could you tell us about that?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REBIHIC
utterances.text: When the commission was assigned the task to carry out the exchange, we immediately started working on it, so that representatives of both the army and the HVO had interviews with the prisoners held by the army in Stari Vitez, and the brigade commander in Preocica, Mr. Kelestura, was instructed to prepare the prisoners for exchange, the prisoners held by the army within the area of responsibility of the brigade. We compiled that list and we from Stari Vitez completed this immediately. However, it is important to note something in relation to that meeting. I remember very well that at that meeting Mr. Cerkez even then alleged that he had no prisoners. On the basis of that, we immediately released the prisoners that were held in the TO headquarters in Stari Vitez. When we arrived in Vitez, that is, all the members of the commission, in the cinema hall we found 13 detainees, Muslim detainees, mostly intellectuals from Vitez, who had been kept on after a previous release. I think this was the 30th of April when Sefer and Mr. Petkovic were present. They were taken from the Workers' University to the premises of the SDK, the social accounting service, and after that to Kaonik. We arrived at the Workers' University building where we found these 13 prisoners and I addressed on that occasion Mr. Mario, asking him, "You said they were released, but they are still in detention." Mario replied that they were safer there than in their own apartments. Mario went to his office and, together with the other members of the commission, I worked in accordance with the tasks assigned to us and I asked that each of the prisoners should state clearly whether he wished to remain on the territory of Vitez under HVO control, of course that is implied, or whether they wished to be taken out, simply relocated to the free territory under the control of the BiH army. With the exception of two detainees, all the others wanted to leave Vitez. And, of course, they wanted their families to be allowed to leave as well. At one point, a misunderstanding arose, because Mario would not allow families to go as well, though he was present at the UNPROFOR base when this particular point had been arranged as well. I reminded Mr. Mario Cerkez of those agreements that we had had, and that if he would not abide by them, I said nothing would come of the exchange, but that I would inform representatives of UNPROFOR and the ECMM of this. After that permission was given. So the next day, those detainees were evacuated to Poculica, and from Poculica prisoners were released that were detained by the BiH army or, more specifically, the 325th Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: The document that I wish to show you now, Mr. Rebihic, is a document drawn up on the occasion of the release of these 13 detainees. Could you please tell me whether you recognise this document as being issued by you, the 24th of May, 1993, Z27212, which has already been tendered through another witness; 27112.

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REBIHIC
utterances.text: Yes, the whole commission worked on this document, as specified by the signatures of Jozic Borislav, Hajdarevic Refik, Stipo Krizanac, and under number 4 is my signature. Yes, that is that document.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: A point of clarification, Mr. Rebihic. Borislav Jozic, or Boro, was he an officer of the Vitez Brigade?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REBIHIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: And Mario Cerkez was his superior?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REBIHIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: In the course of the second half of 1993 you remained in Stari Vitez, which was under siege. When exactly was the siege lifted from Stari Vitez?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REBIHIC
utterances.text: The siege was lifted with the signing of the Washington Accord, the 25th or the 27th of February, 1994. I'm not sure of the date, but, in any event, after the Washington agreements were signed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: Could you tell us what the living conditions were in Stari Vitez during that time of siege?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REBIHIC
utterances.text: Being totally encircled and hopeless and living in uncertainty, I think speaks for itself. It was very, very hard. We had no reserves of food or fuel, so that shortages of essential foodstuffs appeared very soon.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: You were also exposed constantly to fire from HVO forces that encircled you?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REBIHIC
utterances.text: Yes. I was just going to say that. Throughout this period, we were constantly exposed to fire, either shelling or handmade grenades -- we called them "babies" -- or shells coming from artillery. There were frequent attacks and frequent instances of people being wounded, and the HVO would not allow timely intervention in terms of evacuating the injured and treating them in hospitals, so that quite a number of people were killed because they were not treated on time. A number of them were killed by snipers, among whom were old people, women, children. If you want the numbers, it is a figure that is deeply embedded in my memory. Throughout that period, 54 people were killed, out of which 29 were able-bodied men. The others were elderly, women, and children. There were cases that one such "baby", as it was popularly known, several people would be killed and many more injured.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: Would you please speak to us about the 18th of June [as interpreted], 1993, when Stari Vitez was severely attacked by the HVO? On that day, Stari Vitez was attacked from many sides by different forces that were conducting a joint operation?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REBIHIC
utterances.text: I think it was the 18th of July, not the 17th, of 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: Just a moment, please. In the transcript, by error it says "the 18th of June", but let's make it quite clear it's the 18th of July that we're talking about.

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REBIHIC
utterances.text: Yes, July. May I begin?

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: Yes. Continue, please.

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REBIHIC
utterances.text: It is the second strongest attack carried out against Stari Vitez in terms of effectives and force. Early in the morning, this attack started before 5.00 a.m. perhaps, and we did have some indication that there would be an attack because we had information that an armoured vehicle, a personnel carrier that had been made by hand, it was to be sent by the HVO to break up the defences of Stari Vitez from within. This personnel carrier, made out of a bulldozer, it was really a Caterpillar bulldozer, TG-190, in the course of the night it was transported from the factory compound to the plateau in front of the Catholic church in Stari Vitez. We heard that quite clearly, and we could see its lights when it was moving towards that position.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: What were the units that participated in that attack on Stari Vitez?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REBIHIC
utterances.text: All HVO units took part in this attack, including the military police, and Vitezovi, and Jokers. There were units who were not from the Vitez territory and even those who were not from the territory of Bosnia-Herzegovina, which we identified and determined through a document which we found on one of the killed soldiers while clearing the area, removing the bodies of the killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: Do you remember that soldier's name?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REBIHIC
utterances.text: I do recall it. His name was Slavko Jankovic. I believe he had a military identity card which identified him as a member of the Zengas, and I believe that he came from the area of the town of Osijek.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: It was the Croatian army, the Republic of Croatia; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REBIHIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, that is what the identity card clearly reflected.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: During the attack, the Vitez Brigade participated in the action; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REBIHIC
utterances.text: Yes, certainly.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: Do you remember that several HVO soldiers died on that day? Would you remember the names of some of those soldiers?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REBIHIC
utterances.text: Yes. Four or several soldiers were caught up on the line, directly adjoining the lines, the ABiH; Zoran Sero, Zlatko Nakic, a member of the military police, Neven Kovac, and I believe another person from the Vitez area -- I cannot recall his name -- and another person I had already referred to.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: You speak about the military police in Vitez. Which military police are you talking about, the regional police or the Vitez Brigade military police?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REBIHIC
utterances.text: The Vitez Brigade of the HVO, because Zlatko Nakic was obviously a part of that unit because he also was an escort to the commission to which I have previously referred.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: You were a military man in the former Yugoslavia People's Army, that is, in the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina, Mr. Rebihic?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REBIHIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: Do you know what instructions are provided by the rules of those armies in respect of concerted operations which are conducted by special units within a sector for which the brigade commander has responsibility?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REBIHIC
utterances.text: In the area of responsibility, it is the commander of the largest formation that is responsible in that zone of responsibility. All other units are attached to him, and all the operations are coordinated in accordance with the tasks and situation and the specific combat task.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: In respect of the Vitez zone, Mario Cerkez, as the brigade commander, was the person responsible for the Vitez sector?

utterances.speaker: NIHAD REBIHIC
utterances.text: Yes. That was the zone of responsibility of the HVO Vitez Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I have no further questions, Mr. President. Just one moment, please, Mr. President. Mr. President, Mr. Nice has reminded me that it might be appropriate or possible tomorrow, once the Defence has seen the witness's diaries, that the question of the chronology and timing, which was mentioned by the witness in that diary at the time, be gone back into.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: It seemed to me to be fairly clear, but we'll see how things go tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, with your permission, if I can make a comment on the diary.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Well, what do you want to say about it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I clearly stated to the Prosecutor that I was willing to turn over my personal diary, make it available, in order for it to make a comparison of the authenticity of the excerpts, which I provided in copy, with the original that is in my possession. The same offer goes for the Defence. Anything I had enclosed in the excerpts can be compared to the documents which I have in the original.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. Just before we finish, one housekeeping matter. The sittings for November will be altered to this extent: that because of the requirements of other cases, we shall not be sitting in the afternoons of the 1st to the 5th of November, the afternoon of the 23rd of November, and the morning of the 11th of November. It's unfortunate that these other cases require us to be elsewhere, but that is the position here and the practice as far as the Tribunal is concerned. I hope we'll be able to make up such speed as we can by getting through the witnesses more quickly. Very well. Half past 9.00. Mr. Rebihic, would you be back, please, at half past 9.00 tomorrow, and I hope it will be possible to conclude your evidence tomorrow.
